reading.body:
One row in this data set is not a data center: DataPro USA Web Development is an inactive web design business, mistagged in OpenStreetMap, with zero megawatts and no published specifications.

The evidence points one way. The company's domain is a parked for-sale page. The stored coordinates resolve to a different current occupant, Hole Hunter Industries on East Gray Road in Scottsdale. There is no operator, no website, no megawatt figure, and no equipment specification. The only thing marking this location as infrastructure is a single OpenStreetMap node tagged as a data center.

That matters because facility counts are used as a proxy for available compute and the power that feeds it. A false positive raises the count without adding a watt of load or a square foot of hall. The zero megawatts recorded here is the accurate figure, and the record should be excluded from any tally of AI-relevant capacity. Its location in Maricopa County, 13.3 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor, places it near real data center activity, but proximity to a cluster is not evidence of a facility.

What this does not tell you is anything about Arizona's actual data center capacity or its electricity demand. It is one bad row, not a measurement of a market. It also does not establish when the business stopped operating or whether it ever housed servers. The research is marked exhausted with no independent lead found, so the absence of evidence is the finding.
